headline: Soto's three-run homer lifts Mets past Phillies, 6-3
recap: The Phillies fell 6-3 to the Mets in New York on Friday. New York scored three times in the bottom of the first: Carson Benge's single drove in Francisco Lindor, and A.J. Ewing's single two batters later brought home Bo Bichette and Benge. Bryson Stott's RBI double in the second cut it to 3-1. Edmundo Sosa's solo home run, his eighth, made it 3-2 in the sixth, but Juan Soto answered in the bottom of the inning with a three-run homer, his 26th, scoring Marcus Semien and Luis Torrens to push the Mets lead to 6-2. Derek Hill's solo homer in the seventh, his 11th, closed the scoring. Opener Tim Mayza took the loss after allowing three runs on three hits in a third of an inning; Jose Urquidy followed with four and two-thirds scoreless innings and six strikeouts, and Orion Kerkering was charged with the three runs in the sixth. Zac Thornton worked six innings for the win and Dedniel Nunez threw the final one and a third innings for the save. Sosa went 3-for-3 with the homer, a double and an RBI.
The Phillies are 85-69, second in the NL East, five games behind the first-place Braves. They have lost their last game and carry a one-game losing streak.

Philadelphia continues the series in New York on Saturday, September 19, with Andrew Painter starting opposite the Mets' Christian Scott. First pitch is scheduled for 4:10 PM ET. New York is a moneyline favorite at -126 to Philadelphia's +104, and the run line has the Phillies at +1.5 (-200). The Phillies are off Monday before opening a home series against the Brewers on Tuesday, September 22.
